clue.text: Incenses through displays of rage

parts.note: per is the Latin-derived word for through or by way of
someone who fumes is seething, so fumes are outbursts of anger

explanation.surface: Someone's furious outbursts get people worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incenses' looks like the verb for angering, matching the rage, but here it is the verb for scenting with incense.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense is to fill with fragrant smoke, and to perfume is likewise to scent the air.

clue.text: The French raised some sheep with matted fleece

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the article is read upwards

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the
a flock is a group of sheep

explanation.surface: A French farmer rears sheep whose wool is all tangled.
explanation.definitionFit: An elf-lock is a tangled knot of hair, supposedly the work of mischievous sprites.

clue.text: One way to carry off the Marseillaise?

definitions.text: One way to carry off the Marseillaise?

parts.words: One way to carry off the Marseillaise?
parts.note: the Marseillaise is a French march, and an old slang word for a Frenchman plus march gives a way of hauling someone off by the arms

explanation.surface: A question about how best to perform the French national anthem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carry off' suggests pulling off a performance, but it means hauling someone away with their arms pinned.
explanation.definitionFit: To bundle someone along forcibly with arms held behind them is a standard idiom for this term.

clue.text: Pairing earning a point on board

explanation.surface: Teaming up and scoring on the board game.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals coupling are pairing up; in chess, delivering checkmate wins the game and its point.

clue.text: Heavenly body from the East throwing herself at the mob

indicators.note: throwing the letters tosses them into a new order

explanation.surface: A celestial figure from the Orient hurls herself at a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwing' rearranges HERSELF AT THE MOB, fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The star that guided the Magi from the East to the infant Jesus is a celestial object of legend.

clue.text: Supplies method of punishment

explanation.surface: A punishment involves taking away provisions.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocks are stored provisions or reserves; the stocks were also a wooden frame pinning an offender's feet for public humiliation.

clue.text: Upright reputation

explanation.surface: An honest person's good name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on its feet is erect, not lying down; one's position in others' esteem is also one's status.

clue.text: Spanish river divides family, that's loud and clear

indicators.note: the river splits the family word in two by sitting inside it

parts.note: a clan is a family group
rio is the Spanish word for river

explanation.surface: A river in Spain splits a family, which is plainly obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarion call is ringing and unmistakable, from a shrill medieval trumpet.

clue.text: Resort with precipitous promontory

parts.note: a sheer drop is very steep
ness is a headland, found in place names

explanation.surface: A seaside town has a steep headland.
explanation.walkthrough: SHEERNESS is a town on the Isle of Sheppey in Kent, England.
explanation.definitionFit: This Kentish town on the Thames estuary was once a seaside holiday place.

clue.text: Free of debt, put a sum of money in the till

parts.note: the article a gives the letter A

parts.words: sum of money in the till
parts.note: a float is the cash put in a till at the start of trading to make change

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper solvent at last puts some cash in the register.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that stays afloat is solvent, keeping its head above water financially.

clue.text: Disposal of an obstruction produces water

parts.note: the article an gives the letter A
a dam is a barrier blocking a river
a sale is a disposal of goods for money

explanation.surface: Getting rid of a blockage releases a flow of water.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are read in the order A DAM SALE, the sale of a dam. ADAM'S ALE is a jocular old name for plain water, the only drink in Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's ale is a humorous idiom for drinking water, Adam having had nothing else to drink.

clue.text: Responsibility given to old soldier

parts.note: to have command of something is to be in charge of it

explanation.surface: A veteran trooper is put in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old soldier' looks like one phrase, but 'old' gives only the O and 'soldier' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a member of a specially trained raiding force, so a kind of fighting serviceman.

clue.text: He won't accept! an old coin

explanation.surface: A man stubbornly refuses an antique piece of money.
explanation.definitionFit: One who denies something rejects it; a denier was also a small French coin of former times.

clue.text: Woman to avoid''

explanation.surface: Someone warns that a certain female should be steered clear of.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit of skirt is old slang for a female; to skirt an issue is to go round it rather than face it.

clue.text: Weed the site on the corner

parts.note: a seat is a location, as in a seat of government
an angle is a corner

explanation.surface: Weeds grow on the plot at the corner.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea-tangle is a type of seaweed, a kelp.

clue.text: Plenty call for solo

explanation.surface: Lots of people bid to play alone.
explanation.walkthrough: Solo here is solo whist, a card game in which abundance is a bid to win nine tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance means a plentiful supply; in solo whist it is also the bid undertaking to take nine tricks.

clue.text: Still, whatever the speed

explanation.surface: Motionless, however fast one goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Still as in nevertheless is a sentence adverb of concession; literally it is regardless of pace.

clue.text: Model runs in metal groove

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters are moulded into a new form

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A model train runs in a groove of metal track.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramline is the slot in the road in which a tram's rail runs, so a channel.

clue.text: A solitary' spin round in the car

indicators.note: to spin letters is to whirl them about into a new order

parts.note: a round shape is a circle, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A lonely person goes for a drive round and round in the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin' rearranges O (round) with IN, THE and CAR, nine letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary as a noun is a hermit or recluse who lives alone for religious reasons.

clue.text: Stud made from jewel

explanation.surface: An earring stud is made from a precious stone.
explanation.walkthrough: A cat's-eye is a reflecting road stud marking lanes in Britain, and also a gem with a slit of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflective studs set in roads are so named; the term is also a chatoyant gemstone.

clue.text: Measurement of magnetism of no use in the atmosphere

indicators.note: the useless item is placed within the air around it

parts.note: the atmosphere is the gas around the earth
US is short for unserviceable, meaning broken or useless

explanation.surface: Measuring magnetic fields in the air turns out to be pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: U/S, for unserviceable, is British military and everyday slang for useless.
explanation.definitionFit: The gauss is the unit of magnetic flux density, named after the German mathematician.

clue.text: Resting, fuddled by drink of whisky

indicators.note: fuddled means confused by drink, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Someone lying down is befuddled by spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A stinger is a cocktail, here a whisky-based mixed drink.

clue.text: Rugby followers

explanation.surface: Fans of the oval-ball game.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is the English public school where the game began.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby is a famous English public academy; a group of disciples of one thinker forms a school of thought.

clue.text: Antony and Cleopatra initially had the stomach to accept one sea battle

indicators.note: the opening letters of the two lovers' names are taken
the belly takes one in, so the numeral sits inside the stomach word

parts.note: tum is the informal word for the belly
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Antony and Cleopatra had the nerve to take on a fight at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Actium was the naval battle of 31 BC where Octavian defeated the fleets of the pair.

clue.text: Dixon's favoured place for exercise, it's said

parts.note: someone favoured by fortune is lucky

indicators.note: the gym is heard spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: a gym is a hall for working out

explanation.surface: A man named Dixon has a favourite venue for keeping fit, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: Jim Dixon is the hero of Kingsley Amis's comic novel, so the book is Dixon's.
explanation.definitionFit: Amis's 1954 novel is named after its protagonist, the hapless lecturer Jim Dixon, so it is his book.

clue.text: A bit pale? Sign here for treatment

indicators.note: the letters are processed or worked over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A patient looking peaky is asked to sign a form before being treated.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone off-colour or queasy is said to look green, so slightly so is a little green-tinged.

clue.text: Nowhere to cook in the house?

parts.note: O, a nought, stands for nothing or no
a range is a kitchen stove for cooking

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether there is no place to cook at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nowhere' splits as NO + WHERE: O plus a place to cook. The house is a royal dynasty, the House of Orange of the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Orange is a European royal dynasty, as in William of Orange, and a dynasty is called a house.

clue.text: Come out and join on end of queue

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word queue is used

parts.note: to merge is to combine into one

explanation.surface: Someone steps out and then goes to stand at the back of the line.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to appear or come into view from somewhere hidden.

clue.text: Harbour encircled by children

explanation.surface: Little ones form a ring around a port.
explanation.walkthrough: Mulberry harbours were the floating ports used for the D-Day landings; children go round the mulberry bush in the nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mulberry was a prefabricated wartime harbour; a mulberry bush is what the children circle in the traditional singing game.
